ad_count.label: Demand
ad_count.definition: How many job ads under your filter mentioned this skill (or belong to this role) in the last four weeks.
ad_count.denominator: Not a ratio — a count of job ads
ad_count.method: Each ad is counted once, however many times the skill appears in it.
ad_count.shareLine: {name} appears in {share} of all {den} ads in this filter (share of ads).
ad_count.shareLineGeneric: Divided by all ads in this filter, the same count gives the share of ads — useful for setting aside the whole market rising or falling.

share_of_ads.label: Share of ads
share_of_ads.definition: Of all job ads matching your filter in the last four weeks, the percentage that mention this skill (or belong to this role).
share_of_ads.denominator: All ads matching the same filter
share_of_ads.method: Skill mentions come from the search API’s full-text match plus our skill dictionary on title and summary.

change_4w.label: 4-week change
change_4w.definition: Ads in the last four weeks compared with the four weeks before.
change_4w.unit: Percent change, with the ad counts
change_4w.denominator: Ads in the previous four weeks
change_4w.method: Weekly counts from our own daily snapshots.
change_4w.caveat: Short windows are noisy. We only flag a change when it is at least 25% and at least 10 ads.

growth_12m.label: 12-month change
growth_12m.definition: Ads in the last 12 months compared with the 12 months before.
growth_12m.unit: Percent change, with the ad counts
growth_12m.method: Roles: official occupation-level vacancy series. Skills: our own snapshots once two years are available.
growth_12m.caveat: Occupation series are counted by the government agency, not by us, and can be revised.

entry_level_share.label: Entry-level share
entry_level_share.definition: Of these ads, the percentage aimed at graduates, juniors or interns.
entry_level_share.denominator: All ads matching the filter, at every level
entry_level_share.method: Title and text rules: graduate, grad program, junior, entry level or intern — and not senior, lead, principal or manager.
entry_level_share.caveat: About 1 in 10 ads is classified wrongly in our hand-checked sample.

no_pr_required_share.label: No PR stated
no_pr_required_share.definition: Of these ads, the percentage that do not state a requirement for permanent residency or citizenship.
no_pr_required_share.method: Text rules for phrases like "must have full working rights", "Australian citizen" or "PR or citizen".
no_pr_required_share.caveat: Not stated does not mean you can apply. Many employers expect working rights without saying so.

employer_concentration.label: Employers hiring
employer_concentration.definition: How many different employers posted these ads, and how much of the total came from the five biggest.
employer_concentration.method: Employer names are normalised; recruitment agencies are counted as one employer each.
employer_concentration.caveat: Agencies can hide several real employers behind one name.

salary_median.label: Median salary
salary_median.definition: The middle advertised base salary for this role in the last 12 months.
salary_median.method: Annualised from the ad’s stated range midpoint; hourly and daily rates are converted.
salary_median.caveat: Only a minority of ads state a salary, and senior roles state it less often.

salary_p10_p90.label: Salary range
salary_p10_p90.definition: The advertised salary 10% of ads fall below, and the one 10% of ads sit above.
salary_p10_p90.method: 10th and 90th percentiles of annualised range midpoints.

skill_premium.label: Skill premium
skill_premium.definition: Median advertised salary of ads mentioning this skill, compared with ads for the same roles that don’t.
skill_premium.method: Compared within each role, then averaged by ad volume.
skill_premium.caveat: A premium is a correlation, not a promise. Senior ads mention some skills more often.

remote_share.label: Remote or hybrid
remote_share.definition: Of these ads, the percentage offering remote or hybrid work.
remote_share.denominator: All ads matching the filter, any work mode
remote_share.method: Work-mode rules on text; ads that say nothing count as on-site.
remote_share.caveat: Many ads leave work mode out, so this is likely an undercount.

contract_share.label: Contract share
contract_share.definition: Of these ads, the percentage that are fixed-term or contract roles.
contract_share.method: Contract type from the ad’s structured field, or from text when it is missing.

skills_per_ad.label: Skills per ad
skills_per_ad.definition: The typical number of skills a single ad for this role asks for.
skills_per_ad.method: Median count of distinct dictionary skills found in each ad.

volatility.label: Volatility
volatility.definition: How much the weekly ad count bounces around over the last 12 weeks.
volatility.method: Standard deviation divided by the mean of 12 weekly counts. Under 0.15 is steady.
volatility.caveat: Holiday weeks raise volatility for everything.

Signal.whyBody: A change of at least 25% and at least 10 ads, with enough ads to trust it. Signals describe the market; they don’t tell you what to learn.

Competencies.title: Core competencies
Competencies.illustrative: Illustrative — based on the ASC core competency scale
Competencies.attribution: Framework: Australian Skills Classification, Jobs and Skills Australia
Competencies.notTracked: Every job uses these, so we don’t track demand for them.
Competencies.scaleNote: Levels run from 1 (basic) to 10 (highly complex) and describe how much of each ability the work calls for. They are not a judgement of any person.
Competencies.roleNote: How much of each everyday ability {name} work typically calls for.
Competencies.count: {n, plural, one {# core competency} other {# core competencies}}
Competencies.searchNote: These ten abilities come from the Australian Skills Classification. Every job uses them, so we don’t track demand for them — role pages show how much of each a role calls for.
Competencies.guideLede: The Australian Skills Classification describes work in three layers. We track the two that move with the market — specialist tasks (what you do) and technology tools (what you use). The third layer is ten core competencies that every job uses.

guideLayers.specialist_task: Specialist tasks — work activities such as analysing data or managing projects. Tracked.
guideLayers.technology_tool: Technology tools — named software and platforms such as Excel or AWS. Tracked.
guideLayers.core: Core competencies — the ten abilities below. Not tracked; role pages show them as levels.

digital-engagement.name: Digital engagement
digital-engagement.blurb: Using digital devices, software and online systems to get work done safely.

initiative-innovation.name: Initiative and innovation
initiative-innovation.blurb: Spotting what needs doing and finding new or better ways to do it.

learning.name: Learning
learning.blurb: Picking up new knowledge and skills and applying them at work.

numeracy.name: Numeracy
numeracy.blurb: Working with numbers, measurements and data to make decisions.

oral-communication.name: Oral communication
oral-communication.blurb: Speaking and listening so that information and ideas are understood.

planning-organising.name: Planning and organising
planning-organising.blurb: Setting priorities, managing time and organising tasks and resources.

problem-solving.name: Problem solving
problem-solving.blurb: Working out what is wrong and choosing a way to fix it.

reading.name: Reading
reading.blurb: Understanding written information such as instructions, reports and policies.

teamwork.name: Teamwork
teamwork.blurb: Working with others towards a shared goal.

writing.name: Writing
writing.blurb: Producing written text that is clear for its audience and purpose.

Breakdown.title: Breakdown
Breakdown.captionLines: Median advertised salary by {dimension}, rolling 12 months
Breakdown.stackNote: Bands add up to the total line: every ad sits in exactly one band.
Breakdown.fallback: Breakdown shows Job ads — {metric} can’t be split this way.

method.experience: Read from the years of experience or level an ad asks for (“3+ years”, “senior”). Graduate, junior and intern ads count as Entry; ads that state neither are placed by job title. Some ads will be misread, so treat the bands as approximate.
method.rights: Read from phrases about permanent residency, citizenship, security clearance or visa sponsorship. “Not stated” means the ad doesn’t say — it does not guarantee you can apply.

Breakdown.salaryStated: From {with} of {total} ads that state a salary (last 12 months).
Breakdown.gaps: Gaps mean too few ads in that group state a salary: {buckets}.
